deck: This week, launches and funding highlight contrasting industry dynamics.

stories.head: SpaceX's Transporter-17: A launch amid doubts
stories.body: SpaceX successfully launched Transporter-17, but the future of its rideshare program is under scrutiny, with many questioning its sustainability. This comes as the Pentagon grapples with over-reliance on a single provider, following SpaceX's satellite winning a critical test. The industry is left wondering if SpaceX's dominance can withstand the pressures of competition.
stories.soWhat: If SpaceX can't reassure the market about its rideshare model, we might see a shift in how smaller players approach launches.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M, rides the defense wave
stories.body: True Anomaly secured a $190M Series C round at a $1.6B valuation, signaling strong demand for co-orbital security solutions. This funding reflects a broader trend where defense-related ventures are attracting significant capital, as evidenced by the recent $1.4B budget increase for space resilience. Investors are clearly betting on national security needs driving future growth.
stories.soWhat: When defense budgets swell, expect more startups to pivot toward military applications, leaving pure-play commercial ventures in the dust.

stories.head: Simera Sense wins contract for Canary Islands constellation
stories.body: Simera Sense has landed a contract to provide multispectral imagers for a new constellation aimed at improving disaster response in the Canary Islands. While $1.85M isn't a game-changer, it highlights the increasing importance of satellite technology for local governments addressing climate-related challenges. Even islands need to step up their tech game.
stories.soWhat: If island nations start investing in space tech, it could signal a new wave of market opportunities for small satellite providers.

watchlist.title: SpaceX's rideshare program under pressure

watchlist.title: True Anomaly's defense focus expands

watchlist.title: Isar Aerospace's Canadian launch site plans
watchlist.body: The agreement with Canada could open new markets for Isar Aerospace, especially in defense-related launches.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN extension implications
watchlist.body: The $480M contract extension suggests Palantir's continued dominance in military applications, which may impact competitors.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
